flashcard_questions.q: What does it mean that Christians are monotheistic?
flashcard_questions.a: They believe in only one God.

flashcard_questions.q: What does omnipotent mean as a quality of God?
flashcard_questions.a: All-powerful, with unlimited power and authority.

flashcard_questions.q: What does benevolent mean as a quality of God?
flashcard_questions.a: All-loving and all-good, desiring the best for all people.

flashcard_questions.q: Who spoke the words “Nothing is impossible with God”?
flashcard_questions.a: The angel Gabriel, speaking to the Virgin Mary.

flashcard_questions.q: Which verse do Christians use to show God’s greatest act of love?
flashcard_questions.a: John 3:16 — God gave his one and only Son so believers may have eternal life.

flashcard_questions.q: What does it mean that God is just?
flashcard_questions.a: God is a fair judge who never supports injustice or cruelty.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the problem of evil?
flashcard_questions.a: The challenge of explaining why an all-loving, all-powerful God allows suffering.

flashcard_questions.q: Which philosopher set out the problem of evil in the 1700s?
What name do philosophers give to the three ideas that seem to contradict each other?
What is moral evil in Christian thought?
flashcard_questions.a: Suffering caused by human actions such as murder or war.

flashcard_questions.q: What is natural evil in Christian thought?
flashcard_questions.a: Suffering caused by the natural world, such as earthquakes or disease.

flashcard_questions.q: How does the free will response explain moral evil?
flashcard_questions.a: God gave humans freedom to choose, and some choose to do wrong.

flashcard_questions.q: Which story do Christians use to argue that suffering tests faith?
What is the Trinity in Christian belief?
flashcard_questions.a: One God existing as three equal and eternal persons.

flashcard_questions.q: What happened to the disciples at Pentecost?
flashcard_questions.a: The Holy Spirit descended on them as tongues of fire.

notes: 15 cards: 5 term→definition (monotheistic, omnipotent, benevolent, moral evil, natural evil), 3 argument→view (free will, Job, problem of evil), 3 belief→source (Luke 1:37, John 3:16, Pentecost), 2 attribution (Hume, inconsistent triad), 2 doctrine (God as just, Trinity). Trinity card avoids listing the three persons so it stays one fact.
